mes:
## Blossomtide 14, 348 | Elerian Keep, the morning of departure

The first ten of the fifty riders were waiting under the gatehouse arch, where the shod horses had worn hollows in the stone. Edren called from the baggage wagon that he could get the two spare waterskins into the armor chest if Hale would let him take the greaves out. A groom put Night's bridle over the rail before he went back fo
I walk out to the gatehouse and ask Edren what he is packing.

Edren knelt by the armor chest under the gatehouse arch. "Two spare waterskins fit if the greaves come out," he said. Hale lifted the greaves himself and set them in the baggage wagon. "Then the greaves ride with the flour," Hale said. Edren packed both waterskins into the armor chest and buckled the strap.

mes: I go with Hale to the stable to look at Night.

In the stable Hale ran his hand down Night's left foreleg and lifted the hoof. The foreshoe rocked under his thumb. "Brannic," he called. The smith came with his hammer and reset the left foreshoe with four new nails while Night stamped and blew.

mes: I ask Hale when the General expects us at Crossroads.

General Aldric St. Claire rode into the yard on his grey and did not dismount. "Six days to Crossroads Keep," Aldric said. "Darius has asked for the Vanguard, and I want you at his gate before the new moon." Hale saluted. "Six days, General." Aldric turned his horse toward the gate.

The column passed under the gate at second bell. Ser Marten Drey took the rear guard with ten riders and the baggage wagons. Hale rode at the head with Night fresh under him and Heather on his left.

mes: I ask Hale about the salt mark on his wrist.

Hale turned his wrist so the salt mark caught the light. "My mother put the first one there," he said. "Brenna of Ashen Ford. She said salt keeps a man honest on the road." Heather touched the mark and he let her.

mes: At the midday halt I help Edren water the horses.

They halted at Aldermarch where the road met the river. Edren knelt on the bank to fill the skins and one waterskin slipped from his hands and went downstream. "One left," Edren said, holding up the other. Hale laughed and told him to keep it out of the river.

mes: I ask how far it is to Harren's Cross.
"Half a day yet," Hale said. The road climbed through the alder stands and the riders went quiet in the heat. Night kept an even pace.
We reach Harren's Cross and I follow Hale into the inn.

Harren's Cross was a crossroads with six houses and the Broken Spur. The innkeeper, a broad man named Tobin, met them at the door with a lamp. "Fifty riders," Tobin said. "I have beds for nine and a barn for the rest." Hale paid him for the barn and the nine beds.

Tobin set down two cups. "Lord Darius doubled the toll at Valen Ford last month," he said. "Every rider pays, Vanguard or no." Hale frowned into his cup.

mes: When we reach the ford I watch the toll keeper.
At Valen Ford a toll keeper stood on the bank with a tally stick. "Two silver a rider," he said. Hale counted out a hundred silver from Aldric's purse and the column crossed the river.
On the far bank I ask Edren what he thinks of the toll.
Edren shook water from his hair. "It is robbery," he said. Hale told him to keep his voice down near the toll keeper.
At the evening fire I see Edren with a book.

By the fire Edren had the old calendar book open on his knees, tracing the months of the Elerian Reckoning with his finger. "Blossomtide, then Highsun," he read aloud. Hale corrected his count of the feast days.

v10Changes.text: Edren is Hale's squire. He is learning to read the Elerian Reckoning.

mes: I sit beside Hale and ask if he is worried.
Hale did not answer at once. He watched the dark tree line and then looked at Heather. "I worry when you ride on the outside of the column," he said. He pulled her cloak higher on her shoulder.

mes: We make camp at Crying Rock and I go to sleep.
They made camp under Crying Rock where the spring ran out of the stone. Hale set the watch and Heather slept by the fire. The night passed without alarm.

mes: The next morning riders appear from the trees.
Twenty riders came out of the Northwood at first light. Their leader showed the black tower of Crossroads on his shield. "Lord Darius sends his patrol to escort you," he said. Hale lowered his sword.
I ride back to see how the rear guard fared.

At the rear of the column Ser Marten Drey had a bloody rag around his sword arm. "A branch in the dark," Marten said. "It is nothing." The cut was deep enough that he rode with the arm against his chest.

Lord Darius met them in the gate yard in a plain coat. He clasped Hale's arm too long and smiled too widely. "The General's hound," Darius said. "Welcome." Hale returned the grip and said nothing.

v10Changes.text: Darius greets Hale with false warmth and calls him the General's hound.

mes: At supper I listen to what Darius wants.

At supper Darius pushed a ledger across the table. "Three shipments of iron have gone missing on the road to Saltmar," he said. "I want the Vanguard to find out who takes them." Hale read the dates twice.

mes: After supper I walk the walls and find something.

On the wall walk Heather found a courier's satchel caught in the crenels. Inside was a dispatch with a salt mark pressed into the wax. Hale turned it over in his fingers. "That is no mark of my mother's," he said.

mes: I ask Edren whether he still has water for the horses.
Edren lifted the last waterskin from the armor chest and shook it. "Half full," he said. He filled Night's bucket from it.

scene.where: the wall walk of Crossroads Keep

mes: I ask about the toll we paid at the ford.
Hale snorted. "A hundred silver of the General's money," he said. "Darius will hear about it."

mes: I suggest we ride the Saltmar road at dawn.
Hale agreed. "Ten riders and Jory," he said. "We go to the third mile and we look." He sent Edren to wake Jory.

mes: At dawn I ride with the patrol.
The patrol left before the bells. Jory rode ahead with the scouts and Hale kept Night to a walk on the frozen ruts of the Saltmar road.

mes: At the third mile I look for tracks.
At the third mile the ruts left the road and ran into a gully. Broken crates lay at the bottom with iron bars still inside. Jory whistled.
